complexity.correctness_reason: Instantiating PrefixTree raises NameError on any input because sys.setrecursionlimit is called without importing sys; even with the import added, the fixed 2000 recursion limit would still fail generalized words longer than ~2000 characters.
complexity.notes: sys is referenced in __init__ but never imported. The child-dict keys are single characters from a fixed 26-letter alphabet, so hashing is genuinely constant-time here. Slicing word[1:] at every level copies the remainder of the string, so each operation costs O(L^2) instead of O(L); passing an index into the word, or walking the nodes iteratively with a loop, would restore O(L) per operation and also remove the recursion-depth ceiling that setrecursionlimit(2000) only pushes to a fixed bound. Style: `word[0] not in self.children` is the idiomatic spelling of `not word[0] in self.children`.
complexity.space: O(total characters across all inserted words) for the trie, plus O(L^2) peak temporary space per call from the nested slices and recursion
complexity.summary: Recursive trie: each node holds a dict of child nodes keyed by the next character plus a terminal flag, and insert/search/startsWith recurse on successive one-character slices of the word.
complexity.time_average: O(L^2) per operation, where L is the word/prefix length (each recursive level slices word[1:], copying the remaining string)
